ash: Heads-up: saw a sharp initialization penalty on r-404 during the midnight variant flip — per-token cost spiked ~2.9x for ~17m. traffic steady. looks like KV cache lineage didn't carry and requests hit cold hotpath kernels. Anyone else catch this?
meera: Yep. Heatmap shows cache_hit% collapsed right when canary started. The cost graph looks like a permanent jump which confused PMs.
ben: We should show an explicit "initialization surcharge" overlay on the unit-cost chart for active rollouts. Right now the dashboard only plots raw series so transient surges look permanent. Overlay should include projected surcharge and an uncertainty band.
ryan: Telemetry gap: a lot of token samples don't include route_id or model_variant so attribution during partial canaries is noisy. Propose adding fields: route_id, model_variant, billing_bucket, is_canary, sample_weight, route_owner. Example event (plain text):
```
token_sample route=r-404 model=orca-12k-initv2 billing_bucket=sku-a500-hot cache_hit=false tokens=16 is_canary=true sample_weight=10 route_owner=team-search
```
ux-squad: UX idea: rollout modal gets a small card: "Init surcharge (30/60/120m): $ / tk (proj)" + toggle "auto-pause if cost > baseline * X" + a "token escrow" field where engineers can set a token burn cap for the canary. If projected burn > escrow UI suggests lowering canary pct.
ash: (typo, ignore)
meera: For stats: during the warm window we should upweight canary events (either upsampling or increasing sample_weight) by x4-x7 to reduce bootstrap variance. Alternatively only upweight cache_miss events which carry most signal. We'll include recommended multipliers in the RFC.
ben: Backend: propose an internal endpoint `/internal/init_forecast` that accepts recent token samples + canary_pct and returns `{projected_unit_cost, init_minutes, sku_mix}`. Keep response compact; console will poll every 30s while rollout is active.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started route=r-404 -> orca-12k-initv2 (canary=9%)
ryan: Implementation note: to save ingest cost prefer increasing sample_weight on the client side for canary-tagged samples instead of full additional sampling. Aggregator multiplies counts by sample_weight. Forecast can be a lightweight AR model over cache_hit trajectory + SKU mix. Target compute latency <10s for smooth UX.
ux-squad: Also add a short inline explainer in the modal: "how we amortize cache savings" with a one-paragraph example showing tokens saved over the init window. Helps PMs not overreact.
